texts: You must have the rights to what you upload

Veyrnox.ai turns text prompts and uploaded files into images, video, speech and music, and lets approved creators submit work to Social Cinema. These rules apply to every prompt, upload, output and publication and form part of the Terms . Social Cinema submissions also follow the Cinema Content Policy .

Before you upload a photo, a video or a recording of a voice, you must either own it or have the permission of everyone identifiable in it. When a generation takes an upload, we ask you to confirm that, and we record the confirmation against that job. Confirming it falsely is a breach of these terms.

Everything this service produces is AI-generated. If you publish it somewhere that expects real footage, say that it is AI-generated. Some jurisdictions, including the EU under the AI Act, require that disclosure.
We update this policy as the service changes. The date at the top of the page is the version in force.

This policy applies to every title, episode, poster, subtitle, audio track, description and other file submitted to Social Cinema. It is part of our Terms and Acceptable Use Policy .
Creators must choose a label and declare every applicable content warning. These are Veyrnox guidance labels, not official BBFC classifications or BBFC symbols.

Submissions remain private while automated systems examine metadata, images, sampled video frames, speech or captions, file structure and malware signals. A submission may be sent to a trained reviewer. Automated checks can be wrong, so they assist rather than replace human decisions for uncertain cases.

We may reject, restrict, suspend or remove content, preserve an audit record, and restrict or close accounts for serious or repeated breaches. We may report suspected illegal content where required by law. We do not publish a title when a required check is missing, unavailable or unresolved.
We do not make decisions with legal or similarly significant effects about you solely by automated means. Content-safety filtering may block a generation; you can ask us to review a block.

We do not currently embed content credentials or provenance metadata in generated files, so no personal data of yours is carried inside an output by us. A model provider may embed its own watermark or identifier; that is outside our control and we do not add one on top.
UK: Information Commissioner's Office, ico.org.uk. EU: your local supervisory authority. We would appreciate the chance to resolve any concern first.

We do not use data obtained through the YouTube API to train AI models or for advertising targeting. Veyrnox.ai Publish's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy , including its Limited Use requirements.

We will enable these models only after the applicable data-processing and international-transfer arrangements are in place. We will update this notice when the models become available.

Some records stay after deletion, with your name and email removed: credit and payment records (kept for the period tax law requires), content reports and appeals, and referral accounting. They are attached to an anonymous identifier, not to you.

You can access, correct, export or delete your data, and object to or restrict certain processing. See GDPR & Data Rights for how. You may also complain to the UK Information Commissioner's Office or your local supervisory authority.

If you join through someone's referral link, we record which account referred yours. That person can see how many friends joined through their link and is never told who you are. This page explains refunds for generations, Credit Packs, Credit Subscriptions, the Veyrnox.ai Publish Plan and Cinema Pass.
Once a generation completes and the output is delivered, the credits are spent. We cannot refund completed generations because the underlying model provider has already charged us for the compute.
The 10 credits granted on sign-up have no cash value, are not refundable in money, and expire 90 days after they are granted if unused. Purchased credits never expire.
Refund requests that indicate abuse of the free-credit grant or the service may be declined.

Veyrnox.ai is a credit-metered service for generating images, video and audio with third-party AI models. Every generation shows its credit cost before you confirm. We may add, remove or re-price models at any time; the price shown at the moment you generate is the price you pay.
No scraping, reverse-engineering, rate-limit evasion, or reselling access without a written agreement. We may throttle or suspend accounts that put the service or other users at risk.
The service depends on third-party model providers and may be interrupted. We do not promise uninterrupted access. Failed generations are refunded; nothing more is owed for downtime.

Some free Social Cinema series play through the official YouTube embedded player. YouTube remains the source of those videos, and your use of that player is also governed by the YouTube Terms of Service . We may remove an embedded title if its creator disables embedding or removes the source video.

Approved creators must follow the Cinema Content Policy , choose an accurate Veyrnox audience label, declare relevant content warnings, and submit only files they reasonably believe are safe. Veyrnox labels are guidance and are not official BBFC classifications. Submission does not guarantee publication.

Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law. Otherwise, our total liability to you in any 12-month period is limited to the amount you paid us in that period. We are not liable for indirect or consequential loss.
If you are a consumer in the UK or EU, your statutory rights are not affected by these terms.

We may update these terms; material changes will be announced on the site at least 14 days before they take effect. You may close your account at any time. We may terminate for breach with notice where practicable.

Prices are in USD and exclude tax. Stripe, Inc. is the Merchant of Record for credit pack purchases and charges and remits any VAT or sales tax for your location; your total including tax is shown at checkout before you pay.

What users reported, child sexual abuse first. A report about a generation links to the account it belongs to: record the warning, takedown or escalation there ( docs/agents/csam-escalation.md ), then close the report here with a note. Reporters are not told the outcome.

Rules read the signals we already keep (webhook refusals, account freezes, refused sign-ins, admin access refusals) every five minutes and raise one alert per rule, source and hour. Tags are MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Refused sign-ins and admin refusals are recorded while the SECURITY_EVENTS_HASH_KEY secret is set.

Every credit movement on one account, with the reason the ledger recorded, and the append-only action log. Content warnings and takedowns are recorded on the violations page .

Child sexual abuse material. This stops the files being served, keeps them on an evidence hold for the report, freezes the account and sends no email. Then follow docs/agents/csam-escalation.md: IWF or NCMEC within 24 hours.

Every delivery a provider sent us and how we answered. A refusal class names its fix. An event that was accepted but never marked processed means the handler died after the dedupe insert: the provider should redeliver, or the sweep refunds it.
